```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Time to a paying customer: Idea A handles PHI, so it needs signed BAAs, a documented risk assessment and audited infrastructure before any therapist can lawfully use it. Its brief sources a year-one compliance cost of $8,000-$25,000. That is a hard gate against a 90-day, one-person timeline. Idea B has no comparable regulatory barrier to a first sale.",
    "Demand fit: Idea B cites three named SaaS operators (Endcrawl, BurnRate, Hampton), sourced, describing both the pain of manual swag shipping and the value of trigger-based welcome kits. Idea A's sourced complaints are about incumbent pricing and group-practice friction. Its own brief concedes that none point to an unmet need for a minimal notes and reminders app.",
    "Selling motion: Idea B sells to B2B SaaS founders and marketing teams, who can be reached through a free Stripe/Zapier marketplace listing and search ads at a sourced ~$3-6 CPC. Idea A's paid channel has a sourced $500/mo Capterra minimum. Its free channel, r/therapists, is constrained by self-promotion norms and unproven for conversion.",
    "Both ideas face entrenched incumbents. Idea B can be built as a thin wrapper over outsourced fulfillment, which keeps build and ops risk lower. Idea A requires owning a secure system of record for clinical data, with ongoing HIPAA obligations and outsized liability if it fails.",
    "Idea B's biggest weakness is that SwagUp+Zapier already delivers the exact mechanic. That hurts defensibility more than it hurts landing one paying customer in 90 days, which is the stated goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence does not support the product proposed. The Reddit and Oasys quotes ('overkill', 'criminal' pricing, 'expensive for what it offers') are complaints about SimplePractice's price and point toward switching to other full EHRs. They are not evidence that therapists want a stripped-down notes and reminders tool. Several competitive pricing claims in Idea A also count as missing: TheraSoft $69/mo, TheraFocus $199/mo, and the third-party $29 SimplePractice tier have no sources.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs argue against their own idea. Idea B's demand quotes come mostly from vendor case studies and customer stories, which are marketing material. Its customs-friction anecdote and its $60-220 kit-cost figure have no URLs, so they count as missing. The unit economics for low-ACV signups are unresolved. Idea B wins mainly because Idea A's HIPAA compliance burden is a sourced, concrete obstacle to a first paid customer within 90 days, not because Idea B's evidence is strong."
}
```
